ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Babe Didrikson Zaharias

code.originalText: Restaging after four doses: pelvic MRI and endoscopy, immune-related hypothyroidism, and the decision to continue PD-1 blockade

text.paragraph: Restaging after four doses of dostarlimab, and tiredness with cold hands. [S]

Ms. Didrikson Zaharias comes on the day of her fifth dose, after restaging MRI and sigmoidoscopy last week. The cold she had in early June cleared within a week and she had cycle 4 on time. Over the last month she has become tired again, with cold hands on the course, dry skin and slightly heavier legs; her weight is up 0.8 kg. At the sick visit four weeks ago the TSH was 5.8 mIU/L with a normal free T4. Her bowel movements are normal, with no bleeding, and she has had no diarrhea, rash, cough or breathlessness. Sex is comfortable again. She is playing 18 holes and has entered a club competition next month. [S]

list.item:
Low rectal adenocarcinoma, mismatch repair deficient, on dostarlimab (C20). Near-complete response after four doses: MRI shows fibrosis replacing most of the tumor with a small focus of possible residual tumor at the lower margin and normal-sized nodes; sigmoidoscopy shows a flat scar with a small shallow ulcer; CEA 2.1 ng/mL, now normal. Biopsy of the scar was not taken, since a negative result would not change the plan. Treatment continues to nine doses, as planned, with final restaging after the last dose. [S]
Dostarlimab cycle 5 today; cycles 6 to 9 as booked.
Final restaging MRI, CT, sigmoidoscopy and examination after cycle 9.

Immune-related primary hypothyroidism, grade 2 (E03.2). TSH 12.6 mIU/L with free T4 0.6 ng/dL, after a mild rise to 5.8 four weeks ago, with tiredness, cold hands, dry skin and a pulse of 60: primary hypothyroidism from immune thyroiditis caused by dostarlimab. The TSH is high, so this is thyroid failure, not pituitary inflammation, and a cortisol test is not needed. Under the ASCO guideline, immunotherapy continues and thyroid hormone is replaced; this kind of hypothyroidism is usually permanent. [S]
Levothyroxine 75 micrograms each morning, four hours apart from iron.
TSH and free T4 in six weeks.
Dostarlimab continues.

Iron deficiency anemia from rectal blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, now normal, with no bleeding for two months. The ferritin due at three months was not drawn. [S]
Continue ferrous sulfate for three months after the hemoglobin became normal.
Ferritin with the final restaging blood tests.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (J06.9). Resolved within a week; no pneumonitis. [S]
Problem resolved.
